data.rationale: The single-device assumption behind local SQLite doesn't hold: the beta survey shows most hikers already use TrailKeeper on their phone and the web dashboard, and a fifth of them lost photos or edits made on the other device. Postgres with a per-user sync log lets both surfaces read and write the same trip; we accept running one small managed instance in exchange for not losing anyone's trip again.

rejected_options.label: Keep SQLite and add a manual export/import

rests_on.label: Beta survey, Sept 2026: 61% of 140 respondents use TrailKeeper on both phone and web; 22% reported a trip missing photos or edits made on the other device

data.title: Move hike log storage to a hosted Postgres, synced across devices

data.question: Where do we store a hiker's trip logs?
data.quote: Let's not stand up a backend before we know anyone wants this.
data.rationale: TrailKeeper v1 is single-device: one hiker records one trip on one phone. SQLite needs no server, keeps the app fully usable with no signal on trail, and keeps hosting cost at zero while we find out if anyone wants this at all.

rejected_options.label: A hosted database from day one

rests_on.label: Each hiker uses TrailKeeper from a single phone; nobody needs the same trip log on two devices

data.rationale: A second knife identical to the one in evidence turned up two blocks from the apartment, undercutting the claim it was one of a kind. The re-enactment showed the upstairs witness could not have reached his door in time to see what he described. And the only eyewitness needed glasses she was not wearing in bed. None of this proves innocence, but it is enough reasonable doubt that all twelve of us can no longer say guilty beyond it.

rests_on.label: The woman across the street testified she saw the stabbing through the windows of a passing elevated train, but she was also seen with fresh marks on her nose from eyeglasses — she would not have been wearing them in bed, and without them an identification across the street at night is unreliable.

Re-enactment in the jury room: walking from the bed to the front door in the defendant's apartment takes 41 seconds using his own cane, not the 15 seconds the old man upstairs claimed for hearing the threat, running to the door, and seeing the defendant flee.

data.title: The jury finds the defendant not guilty

data.question: How do we avoid a database round trip on every dispatch lookup?

data.question: How do we avoid blocking cold start on a profile fetch?

data.rationale: The 2026-09-20 platform migration reassigned numeric driver ids for over a thousand accounts and briefly served two drivers each other's cached profile. The dispatch service already receives a separate UUID from the identity provider that survives a backend migration; keying the cache on that UUID removes the failure mode the numeric-id assumption depended on.

rejected_options.label: Redis cache keyed by the UUID

rests_on.label: Incident review, 2026-09-20: migrating dispatch to the new fleet-partner platform reassigned driver_id for about 1,200 accounts during the backfill; two drivers were shown another driver's cached profile for several minutes before the cache expired.

data.title: Cache driver profiles keyed by a stable external UUID instead of the mutable numeric id
